'besetzten französische Truppen das Land im Dezember 1806'; the duke 'begab sich ... mit seiner Familie unter dänischen Schutz nach Altona' (German Friedrich Franz I page). The English Duchy page has only 'In 1806 the territory was overrun by the First French Empire'. The page does not say the duke was deposed.

ledger.note: 1808: the occupation ends with the accession to the Confederation of the Rhine on 22 March 1808. German Friedrich Franz I page: 'Im Juli 1807 konnte der russische Zar Alexander I. ... die Wiedereinsetzung des Herzogs' secure, on condition of joining the Rheinbund; 'Daraufhin trat er am 22. März 1808 als vorletzter deutscher Fürst dem Rheinbund bei' (the Confederation page's table has 'Mecklenburg-Schwerin (duchy) 22 Mar 1808'). The reinstatement was agreed in July 1807 but took effect with the accession; no page says when the French troops left, so the end is bridged to 22 March 1808.

1815: the duchy becomes a grand duchy. 'Established: 14 June 1815, at the Congress of Vienna'; 'At the 1815 Congress of Vienna, Frederick Francis joined the newly established German Confederation' and received the title of grand duke (Duchy page). Colour and dossier continue.

ledger.note: 14 November 1918: the grand duke renounces the throne. 'on 14 November, he was forced to renounce the Mecklenburg throne' (infobox 'German Revolution: 14 November 1918'); 'The grand duchy turned into the Free State of Mecklenburg-Schwerin, a federated state of the Weimar Republic.' Infobox status 'Federal State of the German Empire (1871-1918)'. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

wars.outcome: The duchy was overrun by France in 1806 and joined the Confederation of the Rhine in 1808 (Confederation page: 22 March 1808); no land changed hands.
wars.note: Page wording only: 'In 1806 the territory was overrun by the First French Empire.' The Fourth Coalition article was not opened. Reviewer eu-20-e (2026-11-01): the War of the Fourth Coalition page gives '9 October 1806 - 9 July 1807', so the war ends in 1807; the occupation of the duchy to 1808 stays in the ledger.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: Frederick Francis I became 'the first member of the confederation to abandon Napoleon' and 'in 1813-1814 he fought against France'; no border moved (the Confederation was dissolved by the allies on 4 November 1813).

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: The duke backed Prussia (Grand Duchy page); Mecklenburg-Schwerin joined the North German Confederation in 1867. No Mecklenburg land changed hands.

certainty.note: Cliopatria's outline of the duchy from administrative maps; none of the pages gives a boundary.

Borders of a member state of the German Confederation after the Congress of Vienna; the pages record no change of border, and the outline is the same to within 1 percent of area throughout. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes: REPAIR (batch eu-20-e, 2026-11-01). Cliopatria's Mecklenburg shapes omit the southern strip (Ludwigslust, Parchim, Grabow, Neustadt-Glewe, Lübz, Röbel, Dömitz), which Cliopatria draws as Prussian in 1806 and as no state later; all eleven keyframes are adjust, each the Cliopatria shape of its year plus seven 8 km circles on those towns (six new cells, 54 cells, about 13,660 km2 against 13,161 km2 on the infobox and 13,304 km2 on the German Confederation table). The 1806 and 1809 outlines also lack Wismar (the Duchy page has it regained in 1803), added by a circle. Boizenburg falls in a cell across the Elbe and is left out.
